boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Globe Tavern record (August 18-21, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. Deep Bottom II (VA071) overlaps these dates north of the James, and Reams' Station (VA073) follows on August 25. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads 'Corps (34,300 total)' and the live field zero. Humphreys gives the Army of the Potomac 33,684 effective infantry at this time, says the three Ninth Corps divisions sent to Warren had about 6,000 men, not all available, and that Warren first met only Dearing's cavalry brigade, then Heth with two brigades, then Hill with five brigades under Heth and Mahone on the 19th and his own corps with part of Hoke's on the 21st.
claims.rationale: An undivided total, an army-wide figure and formation lists for different days. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory; NPS says Grant extended his lines west and cut Petersburg's main rail link with Wilmington, forcing a 30-mile wagon haul from Stony Creek Station. Humphreys says no further attempts on Warren's position were made. Lee reports the Fifth Corps defeated with about 2,700 prisoners on the 19th and, on the 21st, the enemy driven to his main works and not dislodged.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Lee's August 20 characterization of the 19th and the recorded result differ in scope; not reconciled.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 5,879 (US 4,279; CS 1,600) and the live field 6,055 (US 4,455; CS 1,600). Humphreys gives Warren's losses as 544 killed and wounded and 392 missing on the 18th and 382 killed and wounded and 2,518 missing on the 19th (1,805 from Crawford's division), and on the 21st 517 prisoners and six flags taken and 211 enemy dead buried; Lee reports 150 prisoners on the 18th, about 2,700 on the 19th and over 300 on the 21st.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Humphreys' day totals, Lee's prisoner counts and the frozen totals are overlapping populations.

open_questions: Warren's, Crawford's, Ayres's and Cutler's reports (Volume XLII Nos. 121, 160, 144, 184), Parke's report, Hill's and Hagood's reports (Nos. 372, 368) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
